## 1. What was read

A further **294** records (20% of the 1,505 this month's harvest returned) carry no abstract and are not research: news, correspondence, editor highlights and obituaries. PubMed types them `Journal Article` and nothing else, so the publication-type filter cannot see them — across the whole index they are 22.7% of it and 35% of `general`, and 3,801 of them are JAMA. !!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: bioinfo +136%, sysbio +25%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months: across the 44 months read, 4 of 33 journals are absent from at least one, worst being *Nat Mach Intell* (20 months missing, 81 papers in total) and *Bioinformatics* (4 months missing, 2,905 papers in total). Every journal on the roster contributed this month. Queried directly, PubMed returns zero for those journal-months too — the holes are in the source, reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest. So a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet, and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Nucleic Acids Res 374, Nature 125, JAMA 119, Science 104, Bioinformatics 72, Lancet 56.

## 3. The evidence that moved it







**Checkpoint blockade was attacked at its own premise, not at a target.**
[41299179](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41299179/) (*Nature*) reports that the inhibitory PD-1 axis
*maintains* high-avidity stem-like CD8 T cells. Every next-generation checkpoint
programme in this corpus is built on the assumption that removing inhibition is
additive; if sustained PD-1 signalling is what preserves the precursor pool that
responses depend on, then more blockade is not more benefit and the design
question changes from which receptor to how much and for how long.

**Anti-TIGIT split rather than died.** [SKYSCRAPER-08](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41449142/) is the one
anti-TIGIT phase 3 in this corpus that reads out positive, in oesophageal
squamous carcinoma; [MORPHEUS-EC](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41449151/) adds no meaningful benefit over
PD-L1 blockade plus chemotherapy in the same month. A class that fails in some
tumours and works in one is a class with an unsolved selection problem, not a
dead one — and [41564381](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41564381/), four months later, argues the first
generation failed on Fc isotype design and so was never properly tested.

**Foundation models were audited from five directions at once, and one of them
won.** Fifty TCR-epitope predictors across twenty-one datasets
[all fail on unseen epitopes](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41315816/); a
[single-hidden-layer contrastive model](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41491253/) beats deep integration
architectures; deep expression models
[only match linear baselines even after personal-genome fine-tuning](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41495833/)
and fail entirely on unseen genes; AlphaFold-class predictors
[fail on flexible and disordered interfaces](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41570803/); leading LLMs score
[near chance on curated TF-target interactions](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41386265/). Against that,
[AlphaGenome](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41606153/) beats the best external models in 25 of 26
variant-effect evaluations. The pattern to hold onto is that the wins are on
sequence-to-function tasks with hard ground truth, and the failures are on tasks
where the evaluation set was constructed by the field being evaluated.

**Cell therapy moved off the manufacturing line.**
[Universal base-edited CAR7 T cells](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41363805/) give off-the-shelf allogeneic
clinical data in T-ALL, and [pTalpha](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41338193/) potentiates solid-tumour
CAR-T through translation-level engineering rather than receptor redesign.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[41611245](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41611245/) (*JITC*) is a post-hoc dissection of why ICOS agonism
did not translate in INDUCE-1. It matters more than a single failed programme:
ICOS is the target whose first-in-human trial appeared in August 2025 as the one
piece of clinical checkpoint activity in a preclinical desert, and it belonged to
the wave *before* the roster being nominated at the time. The clinic testing the
previous fashion while the literature nominates the next one is the mechanism
that produces this thread's divergence, and this card is its post-mortem.

[41482545](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41482545/) (*Nat Immunol*): which neoantigens are seen depends on
efferocytic transfer of dead-cell antigen, not on prediction.
[41506790](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41506790/) (*JITC*): neoepitope prediction algorithms do not
recapitulate clinically observed T-cell responses. Two independent statements in
one month that the prediction layer under personalized vaccines is not measuring
the thing it is used to select on.

[41106379](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41106379/) and [41401810](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41401810/) both land on
`suppressive-population-inversion` — TET2-mutant clonal haematopoiesis improving
checkpoint therapy, and opposing functions for distinct Treg subsets in
colorectal cancer.

### (b) Method credibility

[41193809](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41193809/) (*Nature*): specificity, length and luck drive gene
rankings in association studies, with GWAS and rare-variant burden tests
prioritizing different genes for reasons unrelated to the trait.
[41519776](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41519776/) (*Genome Biol*): in standard spatial differential
expression, false discoveries greatly outnumber true findings. Spatial
transcriptomics is the modality this corpus records the most method papers in,
and this is the first card saying the base test is wrong rather than
suboptimal.
